key_insight: The paper introduces a new bandit setting where arm gaps stay fixed but all means can shift adversarially over time. This lets the learner focus on identifying the best arm reliably even when the overall reward level keeps moving.
problem_solved: It addresses best arm identification in stochastic bandits under "Shifting Means," a nonstandard perturbation model where the relative differences between arms remain stable but a shared time-varying shift can change adversarially each round.
method: Formulate a best-arm identification problem under shifting common means rather than fixed arm rewards.
Develop sampling and decision strategies that exploit the stability of the gaps between arms.
Analyze sample complexity for identifying the best arm with high probability despite adversarial shifts.
impact: This work broadens best-arm identification to more realistic nonstationary settings where absolute rewards drift but relative arm quality remains meaningful. It is useful for practitioners building robust bandit-based decision systems in changing environments.
visual_elements: A diagram showing multiple arms with a common vertical shift applied over time while gaps stay constant
A comparison chart contrasting standard fixed-mean bandits vs. shifting-means bandits
A flowchart of the best-arm identification pipeline: sample, compare gaps, eliminate arms, stop when confident
An icon-based timeline illustrating adversarial shifts across rounds
paper_title: Best Arm Identification for Bandits with Shifting Means
paper_authors: Lukas Zierahn, Wouter M. Koolen, Shubhada Agrawal, Christina Katsimerou, Dirk van der Hoeven
